cells.tense: You're at the door with the pen in hand, and today's arrival is being met while it's still warm.
cells.ask: Take the arrival that's already halfway in and give it twenty minutes on paper before you rate it — then see whether the two of you are moving as one.
cells.core:
Something coming toward you right now gets taken on as yours. You reach for it, you put your name on it, you carry it forward — and connections land because of that, not because of luck or timing. There's nothing to brace for. The meeting is happening at the speed it's happening, and you're inside it.

Whatever you've already said yes to this week, say the yes again out loud and spend twenty minutes on it before the day turns over. The question isn't whether it still sounds good. It's whether writing it down keeps the two of you moving as one — and you'll know by the end of the page.

cells.tense: You're leaning into a meeting that hasn't started, arranging how it'll go before it's here.
cells.ask: Set down one piece of the plan for today — the script, the message you've practically sent — and see what's left when you stop steering it.
cells.core:
An arrival can be met at the speed a body keeps: it shows up, you see it, you step toward it, you let it be as quick or slow as it is. No forecasting required. You don't have to know the ending to be in the room.

What's happening instead is that the handling comes before the landing. The conversation gets rehearsed, the ending gets felt early, something gets steered that didn't ask to be steered — and the bracing lands on you, not on the future. What's coming doesn't need arranging from where you are. Drop one piece of the plan and let the day run at its own pace. It won't feel like slackness once you're inside it.

cells.tense: Your attention is at a door that isn't being walked through while what's arriving waits to be noticed.
cells.ask: Name one thing that's true of what's arriving right now — aloud, to nobody if that suits — and notice whether saying it lands any cleaner than holding it.
cells.core:
Unglamorous is the version that works: something arrives, you notice it, you let a word stick to it. The meeting doesn't need a ceremony and it doesn't need you to be certain first. The arrival and your honest read of it are enough, and you're in the room with it.

What's happening now is that some earlier moment holds more of your attention than this one does, so the meeting keeps getting pushed. Things show up anyway. You don't have to trust what's here to say one true thing about it — tired, annoyed, curious, whatever's actually there — and see if the picture comes clearer said out loud. Nothing to decide afterwards. Say it and see.

cells.tense: You're at the threshold picking what comes in, and the pick is filed under timing, luck, the way things landed.
cells.ask: Go back to the smallest format — one page, one decision, today's date — and put your own name on the pick before you file it away.
cells.core:
Done plainly, the pick stays a pick: what's arriving gets seen, something gets chosen, and the name goes on it without commentary. No performance, no explanation. Just the meeting happening with you in the room, on the record as yours.

What's happening instead is that doors open when you say and stay shut when you say — and the account being given out is that the timing decided. It reads as modesty from the outside, and it leaves the decision looking like something that happened to you. One page, one choice, today's date, your own name at the bottom. Keep it somewhere you'll see it.
